articleSummary: Uganda reports its last Ebola patient tested negative, is healthy, and discharged, with a case fatality rate under 10%. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the outbreak is accelerating, with 2,011 confirmed cases and 754 deaths. WHO Director-General Tedros warns the spread is faster than any prior outbreak; undetected infections may be 2–4 times higher. About 80% of new cases in eastern DRC have unknown transmission. Violence and displacement hinder response; ADF attacks in North Kivu's Beni have killed at least 20 and disrupted access. WHO notes only 40% of the $115 million needed; a $69 million shortfall threatens surveillance, contact tracing, and risk communication; Africa CDC calls it the fastest outbreak yet.

articleSummary: Four children in a public pool swimming class in Hanoi, Vietnam, were confirmed infected with Adenovirus, amid a July cluster of Adenovirus-associated respiratory illness and conjunctivitis reported by the National Pediatric Hospital. Doctors warn that common recreation venues beyond water can drive transmission, highlighting five high-risk areas: public pools, ball pits, plush/toy displays, public toilets, and cinema/gym/changing-room spaces. These settings can spread pathogens such as Adenovirus, RSV, Rotavirus, Norovirus, HPV-related warts, hand-foot-mouth disease, and various skin or gastrointestinal infections, especially where cleaning is inadequate. Emphasis is placed on rigorous infection-control measures, continuous disinfection of surfaces and toys, and promoting hand hygiene. Parents should avoid bringing sick children to public spaces and ensure up-to-date vaccinations (influenza, measles, varicella, hepatitis A, meningococcal, pneumococcus, RSV, Rotavirus) before returning to school.

articleSummary: Four children contracted Adenovirus after swimming together at a public pool in Hanoi, triggering concerns about transmission in public venues. At the Central Pediatrics Hospital, hundreds of children presented with conjunctivitis, sore throat, and respiratory infections linked to Adenovirus; four cases were cross-infected at the same pool. Pediatrician Tran Duc Hau, head of Pediatrics at Tam Anh General Hospital Hanoi, identifies five high-risk touchpoints for cross-infection among children: indoor ball pits; stuffed toys and costumes; cinema, activity gyms, and dressing rooms; public swimming pools; and public restrooms. Contaminated surfaces and inadequate hygiene can spread respiratory, ocular, and gastrointestinal pathogens including Adenovirus, Coxsackie (hand-foot-mouth), RSV, Rotavirus, Norovirus, and HPV-related warts; risk increases with crowding and insufficient cleaning. Emphasizes disinfection, keeping sick children away, and vaccination to reduce outbreaks in schools and communities.
notes: 記事は特定の疫学的異常事態ではなく、一般的な小児感染症予防の医療啓発記事。プールでの4例のアデノウイルス感染はエピソード的事例であり、重大な公衆衛生上の懸念には該当しない。
